goldens.comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
goldens.reasoning: C3 describes the same concurrent reuse race.

goldens.comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

candidates: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:131 - A backup code with any non-empty totpCode logs in without checking the password or the TOTP.. The password check above only runs when `!credentials.totpCode`. The new backup-code branch is checked before the TOTP branch, so a request with `totpCode` set to any value skips the password check, and the TOTP is never verified either. Someone who has only the email and one leaked backup code (for example, from a downloaded or printed list) can post `{email, password:"", totpCode:"x", backupCode:"<code>"}` and get a session. One backup code then replaces both the password and the second factor. Fix: always verify the password when `credentials.backupCode` is used, for example by changing the guard to `user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode)`, or reject requests that send both `totpCode` and `backupCode`.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:135 - Closing the dialog on the backup-codes step leaves 2FA enabled but the UI unaware.. After a successful enable, `onEnable()` now runs only from the backup-codes Close button. If the user dismisses the dialog with Escape or by clicking outside (`onOpenChange`), 2FA is on in the server, but the parent's enabled state never updates, so the switch stays off. `step` also stays at `DisplayBackupCodes`, so the next time the modal opens it shows the old codes screen, not the password step. Fix: call `onEnable()` (or let the parent refetch) as soon as the server confirms the enable. Also reset the step whenever the dialog closes, however it was closed.

packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 - A backup code is used up with an unguarded read-then-write, so two parallel logins can both use it.. The code reads the codes from `user` (fetched earlier), decrypts them, nulls the matching entry and writes the whole list back with no condition. If two requests send the same backup code at the same time, both read the old list, both find the code and both succeed, so a single-use code gives two sessions. The second write can also bring back a code that another concurrent login just used. Fix: do the update conditionally, e.g. `updateMany({ where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }, ... })`, and fail when `count === 0`, or run the read and write in a serializable transaction.

apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:174 - Passing `type="password"` to PasswordField breaks its show/hide toggle.. `PasswordField` spreads `{...props}` onto the input, so the explicit `type="password"` (line 176) probably overrides the type it sets from its visibility state. The eye button would then do nothing. Remove the `type` prop now that this is a `PasswordField`.
